references.text: Luke's own account of the women who came to the tomb early in the morning and found it empty. The Emmaus travelers refer back to this event here: [ref:Luk 24:1-10|Luke 24:1-10].
Matthew's account of the women who went to the tomb early in the morning, were terrified and amazed by the empty tomb and the angel's message: [ref:Matt 28:1-8|Matthew 28:1-8].
Mark's account of the women who came to the tomb very early in the morning and were startled by the angel's message about the resurrection: [ref:Mark 16:1-8|Mark 16:1-8].
John's account of Mary Magdalene, who came to the tomb early while it was still dark and found the stone removed: [ref:Joh 20:1-2|John 20:1-2].

The women told all this to the eleven and to all the others, but the apostles did not believe them – their words seemed like idle talk. This matches what the Emmaus travelers say about the women "terrifying us": [ref:Luk 24:9-11|Luke 24:9-11].

Some of the women who followed Jesus and served him are mentioned already here, among them Mary Magdalene, Joanna, and Susanna: [ref:Luk 8:2-3|Luke 8:2-3]. These were among those who went to the tomb.

The women who had followed Jesus from Galilee saw the tomb and how his body was laid there, and prepared fragrant spices: [ref:Luk 23:55-56|Luke 23:55-56]. It was these women who returned to the tomb early in the morning.
